mainTopic: A חיה on שבת (stages after birth, טבילה, fire for warmth), and caring for one's health after הקזת דם
overview: This amud opens by finishing רב אשי's version of שמואל's ruling about desecrating שבת for a חיה. Then it quotes מר זוטרא's more lenient version, and מרימר rules like מר זוטרא because of ספק נפשות להקל. The גמרא next defines when the 'open womb' period starts and how long it lasts. The נהרדעי combine the numbers 3, 7, and 30 into stages: breaking שבת always, then only on her request, then only through a non-Jew. A separate 30-day teaching of שמואל is explained as a delay before טבילה, which רבא limits to when her husband is away. The גמרא then rules that a fire may be lit on שבת for anyone endangered by cold, in any season. This leads into a long section on הקזת דם: protecting the body outweighs בל תשחית, and a person must eat well afterward. Several stories and tips from the חכמים follow. The amud ends with warnings to avoid wind and to eat before going outside, and that list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רב אשי's version: after the womb closes, no desecration
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי's version of שמואל's ruling ends: once the קבר has closed, we do not desecrate שבת for the חיה, whether or not she says she needs it.
steps.simpleTranslation: …'I need it,' or whether she did not say 'I need it,' we do not desecrate שבת for her. That is how רב אשי taught it.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. We are hearing the end of רב אשי's version of שמואל's ruling about the period after the womb has closed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב אשי's version, once the קבר has closed, her own words no longer matter. Even if she says 'I need it,' we do not desecrate שבת. The closing line 'רב אשי מתני הכי' tells us this was just one way of teaching שמואל's words, and a second version is about to come.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I need it.' The woman says she needs שבת to be desecrated for her.
We desecrate שבת for her sake
He taught it this way. This introduces or closes one version of a teaching.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this sentence is a complete ruling by itself. It is only the second half of רב אשי's version. The first half, about when the womb is still open, came on the previous amud.

phrases.english: …'I need it,' or whether she did not say 'I need it'
phrases.notes: This picks up from the line before: 'once the womb has closed, whether she said…'

phrases.english: we do not desecrate Shabbat for her.
That is how Rav Ashi taught it.
phrases.notes: This wraps up the first version of the teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אשי's version, which began on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per רב אשי: after the קבר closes, we never desecrate שבת for her, even if she says she needs it.

steps.title: מר זוטרא's version: after the womb closes, her request is enough
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא quotes שמואל differently. While the womb is open, we always desecrate שבת for her. After it closes, we desecrate שבת if she says she needs it, and not if she doesn't say so.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא taught it this way: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: For a חיה, as long as the womb is open, whether she says 'I need it' or says 'I don't need it,' we desecrate שבת for her. Once the womb has closed, if she says 'I need it,' we desecrate שבת for her. If she does not say 'I need it,' we do not desecrate שבת for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a second, competing version of the same statement of שמואל, as taught by מר זוטרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree about the time when the womb is open: we always desecrate שבת. The only difference is after the womb closes. רב אשי says no desecration at all, while מר זוטרא says her saying 'I need it' is enough to permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has just given birth or is giving birth
Literally 'the grave is open.' This is a term for the womb being open during and after birth.

steps.whyThisMatters: Two versions of one אמורא's statement that lead to different practical results create a real question of הלכה. That question is resolved in the next steps.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra taught it this way:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A woman in childbirth, as long as the womb is open,
whether she said 'I need it,'
or whether she said 'I don't need it' —
we desecrate Shabbat for her.
Once the womb closed, if she said 'I need it' —
we desecrate Shabbat for her.
If she did not say 'I need it' —
we do not desecrate Shabbat for her.
phrases.notes: And certainly not if she said 'I don't need it'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a rival version of the same statement of שמואל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per מר זוטרא: after the קבר closes, we desecrate שבת if she says she needs it.

steps.title: רבינא asks which version is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks מרימר: מר זוטרא's version is lenient and רב אשי's is strict. Which one do we follow?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to מרימר: מר זוטרא teaches it leniently, and רב אשי teaches it strictly. Whose view is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks a practical question: since there are two versions, which one do we actually follow? This sets up the ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Lenient' and 'strict' here are measured in terms of שבת. מר זוטרא is lenient because he permits desecrating שבת more often, and רב אשי is strict because he permits it less often.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Mareimar:
Mar Zutra teaches leniently,
and Rav Ashi teaches stringently,
the halakha is in accordance with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to decide between the two versions
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical הלכה when the womb has closed and she says she needs it

steps.title: מרימר rules like מר זוטרא because a life may be at stake
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows מר זוטרא, because when there is a doubt about danger to life, we are lenient about שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The הלכה follows מר זוטרא, because in a case of doubt about life, we are lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר answers that we follow מר זוטרא, and he gives the reason: ספק נפשות להקל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know for sure which version is what שמואל really said, so there is a doubt. When a life might be in danger, any doubt is decided in favor of saving the life. That means we desecrate שבת when she says she needs it.

keyTerms.meaning: When there is a doubt about danger to life, we rule leniently, meaning we permit desecrating שבת to save the life

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is like מר זוטרא. After the womb has closed, if the חיה says she needs it, we desecrate שבת for her, because ספק נפשות להקל.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Lenient' (להקל) here means lenient about שבת, which means MORE willing to desecrate it. It does not mean being lenient or careless about her life.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear use of the general rule that a doubt involving life overrides שבת. The same rule applies throughout הלכה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The halakha is in accordance with Mar Zutra,
since in uncertainty regarding life, we are lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Follow מר זוטרא, based on ספק נפשות להקל
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: After the womb has closed, her saying 'I need it' permits desecrating שבת.

steps.title: When does the 'opening of the womb' begin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks from what point the womb is considered 'open', which is when the most lenient rule starts to apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when does the opening of the womb begin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question to define the term 'open womb' used in שמואל's rule. Answers come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that while the womb is open, we desecrate שבת for her even if she says she doesn't need it. So it matters exactly when that period starts.

phrases.english: From when is the opening of the womb?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines a key term from שמואל's ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The starting point of the 'open womb' period

steps.title: אביי: from when she sits on the birthing chair
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the womb counts as open once she sits on the birthing chair.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: From the time she sits on the birthing chair.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first answer: the 'open' period starts when she sits down on the birthing chair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי ties the start of the period to a visible step: the woman takes her position to give birth. From that moment, we desecrate שבת for her with no need for her request.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
From when she sits on the birthing chair.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁתֵּשֵׁב עַל הַמַּשְׁבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of when the womb counts as open
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When she sits on the birthing chair

steps.title: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: from when blood flows, or when friends support her
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the womb counts as open from when blood begins to flow. Another version of his view says it is from when her friends must hold her up by the arms.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: From the time the blood flows down. And some say: From the time her friends carry her by her arms.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different starting point. The גמרא also reports another version of his opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are other signs that labor is truly under way: blood flowing, or her being too weak to walk without help. 'ואמרי לה' means there are two traditions of what רב הונא said.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'open womb' period, when we desecrate שבת for a חיה no matter what she says, begins at a sign of active labor. The signs given are: sitting on the birthing chair, blood flowing, or needing to be held up by others.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
From when the blood flows and descends,
and some say: from when her friends
carry her by her arms.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From when blood flows, or, in another version, from when her friends must support her

steps.title: How long does the open-womb status last?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long after birth the woman keeps her 'open womb' status, which allows breaking שבת for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until when does the 'opening of the womb' last?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא already knows when the open-womb status starts (Steps 6-7). Now it asks when that status ends after she gives birth. This sets up the opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5-7 dealt with the starting point. This question deals with the end point. As long as she is in this status, she is treated as being in danger, and we may break שבת for her.

keyTerms.meaning: The opening of the womb (literally 'of the grave')

steps.confusionAlert: Here קֶבֶר does NOT mean a grave. It is a borrowed word for the womb. The גמרא is asking about the mother's medical state after birth.

phrases.english: Until when is the opening of the womb?
phrases.notes: 'קבר' here refers to the womb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from asking when the open-womb status begins to asking when it ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long after birth the woman remains in the open-womb status that permits breaking שבת.

steps.title: אביי says three days
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the open-womb status lasts three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: three days.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first answer. The status lasts for three days after birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the shortest time period given. According to אביי, after three days she no longer has this special status.

phrases.english: Abaye said: three days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.

steps.title: רבא says seven, or by another version thirty
steps.stepSummary: רבא, quoting רב יהודה, says seven days. Another version of his teaching says thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב יהודה: seven. And some say: thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a longer time than אביי. There is also another report of what was said, which gives thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now have three numbers on the table: 3, 7, and 30. The phrase וְאָמְרִי לַהּ tells us that there are two reports of the same teaching.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה: שִׁבְעָה,
phrases.english: Rava said in the name of Rav Yehuda: seven,
and some say: thirty.
phrases.notes: Another version of the same teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer that gives a longer time period than אביי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Seven days, or by another version, thirty days.

steps.title: The נהרדעי combine 3, 7, and 30 into stages
steps.stepSummary: The נהרדעי teach that all three numbers are correct, and each one marks a different stage. In the first 3 days we always break שבת. From 3 to 7 days we break it only if she says she needs it. From 7 to 30 days we do not break it, but a non-Jew may do the work.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages of Nehardea said: for a woman after childbirth there are three, seven, and thirty days. For three days, whether she says 'I need it' or says 'I don't need it', we break שבת for her. For seven days, if she says 'I need it', we break שבת for her. If she says 'I don't need it', we do not break שבת for her. For thirty days, even if she says 'I need it', we do not break שבת for her, but we have the work done by a non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of picking one number, the נהרדעי use all three numbers to build a ladder. As time passes after the birth, the rules for helping her on שבת become stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first 3 days her danger is assumed, so her own words do not matter. From 3 to 7 days, her own feeling decides. After 7 days she is no longer in danger, so a Jew may not do forbidden work for her. Still, she counts as a sick person, so a non-Jew may do it.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has just given birth

steps.confusionAlert: 'Seven' means the time from day 3 to day 7, and 'thirty' means the time from day 7 to day 30. These numbers are not single days.
steps.whatToRemember: 0-3 days: always break שבת. 3-7 days: break שבת only if she says she needs it. 7-30 days: no breaking שבת by a Jew, only through a non-Jew.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ladder is the practical way the הלכה handles a mother's recovery on שבת, and it brings together all the earlier opinions.

phrases.english: The Sages of Nehardea say:
A woman after childbirth: three, seven, and thirty.
phrases.notes: Three separate stages.

phrases.english: Three: whether she said 'I need it',
or whether she said 'I don't need it',
we break Shabbat for her.
Seven: if she said 'I need it',
we break Shabbat for her;
if she said 'I don't need it',
we do not break Shabbat for her.
Thirty: even if she said 'I need it',
we do not break Shabbat for her,
but we have it done by a non-Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings together the three numbers from Steps 9-10 into one system of stages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 0-3 days: break שבת no matter what she says. 3-7 days: break שבת only if she says she needs it. 7-30 days: no breaking שבת by a Jew, but the work may be done through a non-Jew.

steps.title: The non-Jew rule matches רב עולא and רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the rule for days 7-30 (doing the work through a non-Jew) follows two earlier teachings about a sick person who is not in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רב עולא son of רב עילאי, who said: all the needs of a sick person are done through a non-Jew on שבת. And it follows רב המנונא, for רב המנונא said: for something that has no danger, one tells a non-Jew and he does it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where the last part of the נהרדעי rule comes from. It points to two אמוראים who allow asking a non-Jew to do work for a sick person who is not in danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we may not ask a non-Jew to do forbidden work on שבת (אמירה לנכרי). For a sick person who is not in danger, these אמוראים allow it. After 7 days the mother fits this category: she is still sick, but no longer in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the view of רב...
The needs of a sick person
A situation with no danger to life
One tells a non-Jew and he does it

steps.whyThisMatters: These lines are the source for the הלכה that we may ask a non-Jew to help a חולה שאין בו סכנה (a sick person who is not in danger) on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְרַב עוּלָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב עִילַּאי, דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: In line with Rav Ulla son of Rav Ilai, who said:
all the needs of a sick person
phrases.notes: Meaning a sick person who is not in danger.

phrases.english: are done through a non-Jew on Shabbat;
and in line with Rav Hamnuna, as Rav Hamnuna said:
a matter in which there is no danger —
one tells a non-Jew and he does it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds the final clause of the נהרדעי's ruling in earlier teachings.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that from 7 to 30 days the work is done through a non-Jew.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב עולא בריה דרב עילאי (all needs of a sick person are done through a non-Jew) and רב המנונא (when there is no danger, one tells a non-Jew).

steps.title: שמואל: a woman after birth has a 30-day rule
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל, who says there is a 30-day rule for a woman after childbirth, without saying what it is about.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: for a woman after childbirth, thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching is brought that mentions thirty days for a חיה. It is unclear what it refers to, which sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already saw a 30-day stage for שבת. שמואל's statement is short and does not say which law it is about, so the גמרא will need to explain it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
For a woman after childbirth, thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new, related 30-day teaching about a חיה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman after childbirth has a 30-day period, but the statement does not say which law it applies to.

steps.title: Which law is this 30 days about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what law שמואל's 30 days refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which law the 30 days belongs to. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since שמואל did not name the law, it could seem to be about שבת again. The question makes us look for its real topic.

phrases.english: For what halakha?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what שמואל's statement in Step 13 is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which הלכה the 30-day period of a חיה refers to.

steps.title: The 30 days are about immersion
steps.stepSummary: The נהרדעי explain that שמואל's 30 days refer to טבילה. A woman should not immerse within 30 days of giving birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages of Nehardea said: for immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: The נהרדעי answer that the 30 days are about טבילה, not about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For 30 days after birth she is still weak and could catch a chill from the cold water. So she should wait before immersing. This is a health concern, the same idea behind the שבת stages.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's 30 days for a חיה are about טבילה: because of her weakness, she should not immerse within 30 days of giving birth.

phrases.english: The Sages of Nehardea say: for immersion.
phrases.notes: She is weak and could catch a chill.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 30 days refer to טבילה: she should not immerse within 30 days of giving birth.

steps.title: רבא limits the 30-day rule to when the husband is away
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the rule against טבילה within 30 days applies only when the husband is not with her. If he is with her, he keeps her warm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We only said this rule when her husband is not with her. But if her husband is with her, her husband warms her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to the rule from the last step (no טבילה within 30 days of giving birth). He says it applies only when her husband is not present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger of immersing early is that she will catch a chill. If her husband is with her, he warms her through their being together, so the danger goes away. The rule is not cancelled; it is narrowed to the case where the danger is real.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when… (a formula that limits an earlier rule)

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין בַּעְלָהּ עִמָּהּ,
phrases.english: We only said this when her husband is not with her,
phrases.notes: This refers back to the rule of no immersion within 30 days.

phrases.english: but if her husband is with her —
her husband warms her.
phrases.notes: Through marital closeness, so she will not catch a chill.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין בַּעְלָהּ עִמָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the 30-day טבילה rule given by the נהרדעי in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on טבילה within 30 days applies only when the husband is not with her; if he is, he warms her and she may immerse.

steps.title: The tragic story of רב חסדא's daughter
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's daughter, who was רבא's wife, immersed within 30 days while her husband was away. She caught a chill and died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like this case: the daughter of רב חסדא immersed within thirty days, when her husband was not there, and she caught a chill. They carried her funeral bier after רבא to פומבדיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבא's limit with a real and sad event from his own family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His wife immersed early while רבא was away, caught a chill, and died. Her bier was brought after him to פומבדיתא. The story shows that the danger is real exactly in the case רבא described: early immersion without her husband present.
steps.confusionAlert: This is רבא's own wife. The phrase 'after רבא to פומבדיתא' means she died and her bier was brought to where he was. It does not mean she simply traveled to him.

phrases.english: Like this case of the daughter of Rav Chisda
she immersed within thirty days
not in the presence of her husband, and she caught a chill,
and they brought her bier
phrases.notes: Meaning she died from it.

phrases.english: after Rava to Pumbedita.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates and supports רבא's limit from step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that early immersion is dangerous when the husband is absent.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The death of רב חסדא's daughter after immersing within 30 days while רבא was away.

steps.title: שמואל: make a fire on שבת for a woman after childbirth in the rainy season
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that we may light a fire on שבת for a יולדת during the rainy season.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: We make a fire for a woman after childbirth on שבת in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins. It allows lighting a fire on שבת to warm a יולדת when it is cold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יולדת is treated like someone in danger, and getting cold can be dangerous for her. So lighting a fire, normally a מלאכה, is permitted. The wording mentions only a יולדת and only the rainy season, and the next steps discuss what those details mean.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has just given birth (יוֹלֶדֶת)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
We make a fire for a woman after childbirth on Shabbat
in the rainy season.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: עוֹשִׂין מְדוּרָה לְחַיָּה בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from טבילה to a new topic about the same יולדת: warming her on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may light a fire on שבת for a יולדת in the rainy season.

steps.title: The mistaken narrow reading of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: People concluded that the fire is allowed only for a יולדת, not a sick person, and only in winter, not in summer.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from this: for a יולדת, yes; for a sick person, no. In the rainy season, yes; in the summer, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how people first read שמואל's words. This sets up the rejection that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They treated each detail in שמואל's statement as a limit: only a יולדת, and only in winter. This is a הוה אמינא (first impression). The next step will reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it (introduces a first impression that may be wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not learn this line as the הלכה. It is the view the גמרא is about to reject.

phrases.english: They understood from this:
for a woman after childbirth — yes; for a sick person — no;

phrases.aramaic: בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים — אִין, בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה — לָא.
phrases.english: in the rainy season — yes; in the summer — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a narrow inference from the details in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed reading (later rejected): the fire is permitted only for a יולדת and only in winter.

steps.title: No difference between a יולדת and a sick person, or winter and summer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the narrow reading. A fire is allowed for anyone at risk from cold, in any season.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There is no difference between a יולדת and a sick person, and no difference between the rainy season and the summer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the narrow reading from the last step. Its proof comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל mentioned a יולדת and winter only because that is the common case, not as a limit. What matters is whether the cold puts the person in danger. That can be true for a sick person, and even in summer.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so (rejects a prior assumption)

phrases.english: But that is not so:

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא חַיָּה וְלָא שְׁנָא חוֹלֶה,
phrases.english: there is no difference between a woman after childbirth and a sick person,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים וְלָא שְׁנָא בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה.
phrases.english: and no difference between the rainy season and the summer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, לָא שְׁנָא חַיָּה וְלָא שְׁנָא חוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects both limits: who the person is, and which season it is.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Reading שמואל's example (a יולדת, winter) as a strict condition, when it was only the typical case.

steps.title: Proof: a fire even in תמוז for someone chilled after bloodletting
steps.stepSummary: שמואל himself said we make a fire even in the heat of תמוז for someone who let blood and caught a chill.
steps.simpleTranslation: We know this from what was said: רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of שמואל: If someone let blood and caught a chill, we make a fire for him even in the season of תמוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the rejection in step 20 with another ruling of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone after bloodletting is not a יולדת, and תמוז is the height of summer. Yet שמואל allows a fire. This proves both limits were wrong: the rule covers any person endangered by cold, in any season.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it was stated (introduces a proof)
Let blood (bloodletting, a common medical treatment)
The season of תמוז, i.e., midsummer

steps.whatToRemember: A fire may be lit on שבת for anyone in danger from cold, a יולדת or a sick person, in winter or even in summer.

phrases.english: We know this from what was stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Chiya bar Avin said in the name of Shmuel:
If someone let blood and caught a chill —

phrases.aramaic: עוֹשִׂין לוֹ מְדוּרָה אֲפִילּוּ בִּתְקוּפַת תַּמּוּז.
phrases.english: we make a fire for him even in the season of Tammuz.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאִתְּמַר, אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for the rejection in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That the fire is allowed for a sick person and in summer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's ruling that a person chilled after bloodletting gets a fire even in תמוז.

steps.title: Furniture broken to make fires for שמואל, רב יהודה and רבה
steps.stepSummary: For שמואל they broke a teak armchair, for רב יהודה an ebony table, and for רבה a bench, all to make a fire to warm them.
steps.simpleTranslation: For שמואל they broke up a teak armchair. For רב יהודה they broke up an ebony table. For רבה they broke up a bench.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how great חכמים acted in real life. When they needed warmth after bloodletting and no firewood was available, they burned even expensive furniture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These stories show how seriously the danger of a chill was taken. Even valuable furniture was sacrificed to warm the person. This sets up אביי's objection in the next step.

phrases.english: For Shmuel they broke up an armchair of teak wood,

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה צַלַּחוּ לֵיהּ פָּתוּרָא דְיוֹנָה,
phrases.english: for Rav Yehuda they broke up a table of ebony,
for Rabba they broke up a bench.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows in practice how far the חכמים went to warm someone after bloodletting.
steps.raayaObject: How seriously the danger of a chill after bloodletting was treated.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of שמואל, רב יהודה and רבה, who had furniture burned for warmth.

steps.title: אביי objects: isn't this בל תשחית?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה: by breaking a usable bench, you violated the ban on needless destruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבה: But the master is violating the prohibition of 'בל תשחית' (do not destroy)!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's practice. Destroying a perfectly good bench seems to break the ban on wasting useful things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids destroying useful things (בל תשחית). Breaking up a usable bench for fuel looks like exactly that kind of destruction. אביי is asking how רבה could allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: The ban on wasteful destruction of useful things

phrases.english: And Abaye said to Rabba:
But the master is violating 'do not destroy'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַבָּה: וְהָא קָעָבַר מָר מִשּׁוּם בַּל תַּשְׁחִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice described for רבה in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: Burning a usable bench to make a fire.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Destroying a valuable usable object breaks בל תשחית, so the practice seems forbidden.

steps.title: רבה: not destroying my own body matters more
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that בל תשחית applies to his own body too, and protecting his health comes before saving a bench.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'בל תשחית' of my own body is more important to me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי by turning his own argument around: harming the body is also a kind of destruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not warming himself could ruin his health, which is a far greater loss than a bench. When two kinds of destruction clash, protecting the body wins. So burning the bench is not wasteful; it serves a real need.

keyTerms.meaning: Is more important to me / takes priority for me

steps.whatToRemember: Destroying property to protect one's health is not בל תשחית, because guarding the body is the greater concern.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a lasting principle: בל תשחית forbids only pointless destruction. Using up property for a real need, especially health, is allowed.

phrases.english: He said to him:
'Do not destroy' regarding my own body is more important to me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בַּל תַּשְׁחִית דְּגוּפַאי עֲדִיף לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection from step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing priorities: one type of destruction outweighs another.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning a usable bench is forbidden waste under בל תשחית.
steps.terutzMaskana: Harming one's body is a greater destruction, so using the bench for warmth is justified and not forbidden.

steps.title: Sell your house beams for shoes, and your shoes for a meal after bloodletting
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches a ranking of needs. Shoes come before house beams. A meal after הקזת דם comes before shoes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person should always sell the beams of his house to buy shoes for his feet. If he let blood and has nothing to eat, he should sell the shoes on his feet and use the money for the needs of a meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב about what a person should give up to protect his health. It continues the theme that the body comes before possessions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shoes protect a person from injury and from cold, so they are worth more than the beams holding up his house. After הקזת דם, the body is weak, so eating becomes even more urgent than having shoes. This sets up the next question: what exactly counts as the 'needs of a meal'?

keyTerms.meaning: He let blood (a common medical practice)

steps.whyThisMatters: It extends the lesson from רבה's bench. Guarding your health outranks guarding your property, even something as basic as your house or your shoes.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A person should always sell the beams of his house
and buy shoes for his feet.
phrases.notes: Shoes protect from injury and cold.

phrases.aramaic: הִקִּיז דָּם וְאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכַל —
phrases.english: If he let blood and has nothing to eat,
he should sell the shoes on his feet
and provide from them the needs of a meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of רבה's answer (health before property) with a new teaching about priorities.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shoes outrank house beams; a meal after הקזת דם outranks shoes.

steps.title: What counts as the needs of a meal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'the needs of a meal' means in רב's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are 'the needs of a meal'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question about the phrase it just quoted. It is setting up the dispute that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling your shoes is a big sacrifice, so it must be for something specific. The גמרא wants to know which food is so important after הקזת דם.

phrases.english: What are the needs of a meal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a phrase from step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which food is meant by צרכי סעודה after הקזת דם.

steps.title: Meat or wine
steps.stepSummary: רב says the meal means meat. שמואל says it means wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: meat. And שמואל said: wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two answers to its question. רב says meat and שמואל says wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a disagreement about which food best restores a person after losing blood. The reasons for each view come in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav said: meat,
and Shmuel said: wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: בָּשָׂר, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26 with two opinions.

steps.title: The reasons: life for life, red for red
steps.stepSummary: Meat replaces lost life-strength. Red wine replaces lost red blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said meat, because a soul replaces a soul. שמואל said wine, because red replaces red.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the two opinions and now adds the reason behind each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב thinks the weak person needs meat, a living creature's flesh, to rebuild his life-strength. שמואל thinks red wine is best because it replaces the red blood that was lost. The repetition is not filler; it attaches a reason to each view.

keyTerms.meaning: A soul (life-strength) in place of a soul

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. The גמרא repeats the same two opinions only to give the reason for each one.

phrases.english: Rav said: meat,
a soul in place of a soul.
phrases.notes: Meat restores the person's strength.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: wine,
red in place of red.
phrases.notes: Red wine replaces red blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind each opinion in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat restores life-strength (רב); red wine replaces blood (שמואל).

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming stories
steps.stepSummary: The word שנמסר helps remember the order of the next five Sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: שנמסר.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is a memory aid, not an argument. It sets up the list of stories that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter stands for a Sage in the stories below: ש for שמואל, נ for רבי יוחנן, מ for רב נחמן, ס for רב יוסף, ר for רבא. It helped students remember the order when learning by heart.

phrases.english: (Mnemonic: shenimsar.)
phrases.notes: ש-שמואל, נ-רבי יוחנן, מ-רב נחמן, ס-רב יוסף, ר-רבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the list of stories that follows.

steps.title: שמואל ate a dish of spleen after bloodletting
steps.stepSummary: On the day of his bloodletting, they cooked a spleen dish for שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the day שמואל did 'the thing' (bloodletting), they made him a cooked dish of spleens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins telling how the great Sages recovered after הקזת דם. It starts with what שמואל ate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Doing the thing' is a polite way of saying bloodletting. Spleen is full of blood, so it fits the idea of replacing lost blood. These stories show the Sages really took recovery seriously.

keyTerms.meaning: Did 'the thing', a polite term for bloodletting

phrases.english: Shmuel, on the day he did the thing (bloodletting),
they made him a cooked dish of spleens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First story in the list announced by the mnemonic.
steps.raayaObject: How seriously to treat eating after הקזת דם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's practice of eating a spleen dish.

steps.title: How much wine three Sages drank after bloodletting
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, רב נחמן and רב יוסף each drank large amounts of wine after הקזת דם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן drank until the smell came out of his ears. רב נחמן drank until his spleen floated. רב יוסף drank until the wine came out of the bloodletting cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the stories with three Sages who drank a lot of wine after bloodletting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each description is a vivid way of saying the body was filled with wine. This matches שמואל's view that wine replaces lost blood. The point is to show how important wine was for recovery.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan would drink
until the smell came out of his ears.
And Rav Nachman would drink
until his spleen floated.
Rav Yosef would drink
until it came out of the bloodletting incision.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן שָׁתֵי עַד דְּנָפֵיק תִּיהְיָא מֵאוּנֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of stories, now about wine.
steps.raayaObject: The importance of wine after הקזת דם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practices of רבי יוחנן, רב נחמן and רב יוסף.

steps.title: רבא looked for well-aged wine
steps.stepSummary: רבא searched for wine from a vine that had grown three years of leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא would look for wine that was 'three leaves' old.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the list with רבא, who cared about the quality of the wine, not just the amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Three leaves' means the wine was aged, about three years. רבא believed well-aged wine was best for rebuilding strength after bloodletting. This closes the set of stories.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Of three leaves', i.e., aged about three years

steps.whatToRemember: After הקזת דם, health comes first. You may sell your shoes for a meal. רב says the meal is meat (life for life); שמואל says wine (red for red). The Sages took recovery seriously, eating spleen and drinking much good wine.

phrases.english: Rava would search for wine
of three leaves (aged).
phrases.notes: Wine from a vine that had grown three years of leaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא מְהַדַּר אַחַמְרָא בַּר תְּלָתָא טַרְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final story in the mnemonic list.
steps.raayaObject: The importance of good wine after הקזת דם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's practice of seeking aged wine.

steps.title: Tell your wives an important guest is coming
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks the Sages to tell their wives on their bloodletting day that he is visiting, so a big meal will be prepared.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to the Sages: Please, on the day you let blood, tell your wives, 'נחמן has come to visit us.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the Sages a practical tip so they will get a good meal after bloodletting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps taught that one must eat well after הקזת דם. A wife will cook a large, fancy meal for an important guest like רב נחמן בר יצחק. That way the husband gets the strong food he needs without having to ask for it directly.

keyTerms.meaning: happened to come to us, visited us

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרַבָּנַן:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to the Sages:
I beg of you,
on the day of bloodletting, tell your wives:
phrases.notes: "Your house" is a common Talmudic way of saying "your wife."

phrases.english: "Nachman has come to visit us."
phrases.notes: An important guest means a big meal will be cooked.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of Sages' practices for eating well after bloodletting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using רב נחמן בר יצחק's name as a 'guest' is a fine way to make sure a big meal is prepared after הקזה.

steps.title: The one permitted trick: tasting wine with a worn coin
steps.stepSummary: Tricks are normally forbidden, but a poor person after bloodletting may taste wine in seven shops with a worn coin until he has drunk a רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: All tricks are forbidden except this one, which is allowed: someone who let blood and cannot afford food should take a worn זוז and go to seven shops, until he has tasted a רביעית of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק teaches that deceiving people is normally forbidden, but he allows one special trick for a poor person who needs wine after bloodletting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each shop the person tastes wine like a real buyer. Then he offers a worn coin, which the shopkeeper refuses, so he moves on. After seven shops, the small tastes add up to a רביעית, the amount of wine he needs to recover.

keyTerms.meaning: a worn-out זוז coin that shopkeepers will not accept
a רביעית, a quarter of a לוג of wine

steps.confusionAlert: He is not simply stealing. He really offers payment, and tasting before buying is normal. The shopkeeper is the one who refuses the worn coin. That is why this one trick is permitted when others are not.

phrases.english: And all tricks are forbidden,
except for this trick, which is permitted:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּעָבֵיד מִילְּתָא וְלָא אֶפְשָׁר לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: someone who did "the thing" (bloodletting) and cannot afford food,
phrases.notes: "מילתא" (the thing) is a polite way of referring to bloodletting.

phrases.english: should take a worn zuz
and go to seven shops,
until he has tasted the amount of a quarter-log.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלְּהוּ אִעָרוֹמֵי אֲסִירִי, בַּר מֵהַאי עׇרְמָה דִּשְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב נחמן בר יצחק's advice, now for a poor person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Deceptive tricks are forbidden, except that a poor person after הקזה may taste wine in seven shops with a worn coin until he has had a רביעית.

steps.title: Backup remedy: black dates, oil, and sunshine
steps.stepSummary: If even the wine trick is not possible, he should eat seven black dates, rub oil on his temple, and lie in the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, he should eat seven black dates, rub oil on his temple, and lie in the sun.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a cheaper backup remedy for someone who cannot get wine at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each step down the list is cheaper. First comes a full meal, then free tastes of wine, and finally simple dates, oil, and warmth. The idea of lying in the sun sets up the next story about שמואל.

phrases.english: And if not,
let him eat seven black dates,
and rub oil on his temple,
and lie down in the sun.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a fallback for when the wine trick in step 34 is not possible.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without wine, eat seven black dates, oil the temple, and lie in the sun.

steps.title: אבלט finds שמואל lying in the sun
steps.stepSummary: The scholar אבלט finds שמואל lying in the sun and asks how something harmful can be good. שמואל answers that it is a day of הקזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבלט found שמואל lying in the sun. He said to him: Wise man of the Jews, can something bad become good? שמואל said: It is a day of bloodletting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that seems to show the last remedy in practice: שמואל lying in the sun on a bloodletting day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבלט knew the sun's heat is usually harmful, so he was surprised to see a wise man lying in it. שמואל's answer seems to back up step 35: after הקזה, the sun is good for you.

keyTerms.meaning: אבלט, a non-Jewish scholar who often spoke with שמואל

phrases.english: Ablat found Shmuel
lying in the sun.
He said to him: Wise man of the Jews,
can something bad become good?!
phrases.notes: The sun's heat is normally harmful.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is a day of bloodletting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that seems to support lying in the sun after bloodletting.
steps.raayaObject: That lying in the sun is beneficial after הקזה
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's practice and his answer to אבלט

steps.title: The real reason: the day of תקופת תמוז
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says שמואל's answer was not the true reason. He was really lying in the sun on the day of תקופת תמוז, and he did not want to share that remedy with אבלט.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. Rather, there is one day in the whole year when the sun is most beneficial: the day of תקופת תמוז. שמואל thought: I will not reveal it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the simple reading of the story and explains why שמואל was really lying in the sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story in step 36 seemed to prove that sun is good after הקזה. The גמרא says the true reason was that the sun is especially healthy on the day of תקופת תמוז, the summer solstice. שמואל chose not to reveal that to אבלט, so the story is not a real proof about הקזה. Step 35's advice still stands on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: but that is not so (a rejection of what was just said)
the Tammuz season, the summer solstice
I will not reveal it to him

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not cancelling the advice to lie in the sun after הקזה from step 35. It is only saying that this story was really about a different reason.
steps.whatToRemember: After הקזה, eat well: a big meal, or tastes of wine, or at least black dates, oil, and sun. The story of שמואל and אבלט was really about the special health benefit of the sun on תקופת תמוז.

phrases.english: But that is not so,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִיכָּא יוֹמָא דִּמְעַלֵּי בֵּהּ שִׁמְשָׁא
phrases.english: rather, there is a day on which the sun is beneficial
more than the entire year,
the day on which the Tammuz solstice falls.
And Shmuel thought: I will not reveal it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, אֶלָּא אִיכָּא יוֹמָא דִּמְעַלֵּי בֵּהּ שִׁמְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the simple reading of the story in step 36.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using שמואל's stated reason as the true explanation of the story.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שמואל's answer was a cover. The real reason was the benefit of the sun on תקופת תמוז, which he kept to himself.

steps.title: A memory aid, then: whoever is careless with the bloodletting meal loses Heaven's care
steps.stepSummary: After a סימן for the coming teachings, רב and שמואל teach that a person who is careless with the meal after הקזת דם is treated carelessly by Heaven regarding his food.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Mnemonic: careless, in wind, taste, waited.) It was רב and שמואל who both said: Anyone who is careless about the meal after bloodletting, Heaven is careless about providing his food. Heaven says: He did not care about his own life, so why should I care about him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first gives a short memory aid listing the next few teachings. Then it brings the first one: a person who does not take the meal after bloodletting seriously is punished by Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סימן words match the teachings that follow: הֵיקֵיל = being careless (this step), בְּרוּחַ = wind (the next step), טַעְמָא = tasting before going out, and שָׁהָה = a later teaching. The punishment fits the sin: he was careless with his food, so Heaven is careless with his food. The idea is that ignoring a danger to your own health is a real failing.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid. A list of key words that helps you remember the order of the teachings
One who is careless or takes something lightly

steps.confusionAlert: The parenthesis at the start is not part of the teaching. It is only a memory aid for the next several statements. Each of its words points to a different teaching.

phrases.english: (Careless, in wind, taste, waited — a mnemonic)
phrases.notes: Each word points to one of the upcoming teachings

phrases.english: It was Rav and Shmuel who both said:
Anyone who is careless with the meal after bloodletting —
they are careless toward him about his food from Heaven,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמְרִים: הוּא עַל חַיָּיו לֹא חָס,
phrases.english: and they say: He did not have pity on his own life,
should I have pity on him?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: of course not

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of advice about the meal after הקזת דם, now stressing how serious it is to neglect it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neglecting the meal after bloodletting is careless with one's life, and Heaven answers measure for measure by withholding care for his food.

steps.title: After bloodletting, do not sit in the wind
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל warn that after bloodletting one should not sit in a windy place. The bloodletter may have left him with only a רביעית of blood, and the wind could draw out more and put him in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was רב and שמואל who both said: Someone who has had bloodletting should not sit where the wind blows. Maybe the bloodletter drew a lot and left him with only a quarter-log of blood, and the wind will come and draw out more, and he will come into danger.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second teaching hinted by the סימן (בְּרוּחַ, in wind). It warns against sitting in a draft after bloodletting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the bloodletter may have taken the person right down to the minimum safe amount of blood, a רביעית. If he is already at that limit, a little more loss caused by the wind could become life-threatening. So the rule protects against a case where there is no margin left.

keyTerms.meaning: Does "the thing." A polite way of saying he undergoes bloodletting
At a רביעית (quarter-log), the minimum blood needed to live

phrases.english: It was Rav and Shmuel who both said:
One who does 'the thing' (bloodletting) —
should not sit where the wind blows around,
perhaps the bloodletter drew blood from him heavily
and left him at a quarter-log of blood,
and the wind comes and draws out more from him,
and he comes into danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: הַאי מַאן דְּעָבֵיד מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next teaching in the סימן series: from the meal to avoiding wind
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After bloodletting one must not sit in a draft, because he may be at the minimum blood level and the wind could draw out more.

steps.title: שמואל felt weak when his wall was missing half a brick
steps.stepSummary: שמואל used to do bloodletting in a house with walls seven and a half bricks thick. One day he felt weak, checked, and found half a brick missing. This shows how sensitive a person is to drafts after bloodletting.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל used to do bloodletting in a house whose walls were seven and a half bricks thick. One day he did it and felt weak. He checked and found that one half-brick was missing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about שמואל that backs up the warning against wind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a tiny gap, just half a brick in a very thick wall, let in enough of a draft for שמואל to feel weak. This is real-life support for the rule just taught: after bloodletting, even a little wind is dangerous. It also shows how carefully שמואל himself kept this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Seven bricks and a half-brick, meaning the thickness of the walls
He felt something in himself, i.e., he felt weak

steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows that the danger of wind is not only theory. A great Sage felt it in his own body.

phrases.english: Shmuel was accustomed to do bloodletting
in a house with walls seven and a half bricks thick.
One day he did it,
and he felt weak in himself.
He checked, and one half-brick was missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the previous rule about wind with a story
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one must avoid any wind or draft after bloodletting
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's experience of feeling weak because half a brick was missing from his thick wall

steps.title: Eat something before going outside after bloodletting
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל teach that after bloodletting a person should eat something before going out. If he goes out without eating, meeting a corpse can turn his face green, and meeting a murderer can kill him. The list continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was רב and שמואל who both said: Someone who has had bloodletting should taste something and only then go out. If he does not taste anything, then if he meets a dead body, his face turns green. If he meets someone who killed a person, he dies. If he meets...
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third teaching hinted by the סימן (טַעְמָא, taste). The גמרא starts listing the dangers of going out on an empty stomach after bloodletting, and the list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bloodletting leaves a person weak and very sensitive. Eating first makes him stronger before he faces upsetting or harmful encounters outside. The list is cut off mid-sentence at 'אי פגע' (if he meets), and the next case comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He should taste something (eat a little)
One who killed a person, a murderer

steps.confusionAlert: This passage stops in the middle of the list ('אִי פָּגַע', if he meets). The third case continues in the next part of the daf.

phrases.english: It was Rav and Shmuel who both said:
One who does bloodletting —
should taste something and then go out.
For if he does not taste anything,
if he meets a corpse — his face turns green.

phrases.aramaic: אִי פָּגַע בְּמַאן דְּקָטֵל נַפְשָׁא — מָיֵת.
phrases.english: If he meets one who killed a person — he dies.
If he meets...
phrases.notes: Continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: הַאי מַאן דְּעָבֵיד מִילְּתָא — לִיטְעוֹם מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next teaching in the סימן series: after the wind warning, the advice to eat before going outside
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After bloodletting one should eat something before going outside, because a weakened person who meets harmful sights can be seriously hurt.
